An empty map is not an empty strait. It shows what the receivers can hear.

Reading this map

Why is the strait nearly empty on the map?

The free receivers behind AISStream sit on the coast of Dubai and Sharjah, so they hear the anchorages well and the shipping lanes barely at all. Tankers also switch AIS off near attacks. An empty map does not mean an empty strait.

What do the ship models show?

Tankers are drawn as detailed models, enlarged far beyond true scale so they can be seen, and turned to their reported heading. A vessel without a reported heading is shown as a ring, never with a guessed direction.

How old can a position be?

The feed refreshes every 10 seconds. A position older than 10 minutes fades, and one older than 30 minutes is dropped from the map.

What does the replay show?

Tracks and the replay show positions actually received over the last hour, joined in the order received. Nothing is extrapolated between reports.

How is an AIS gap counted?

A gap is a ship that stops reporting for three hours or more while moving deep inside reliable reception, learned from where at least two different ships are heard nearly every hour. Counting pauses whenever the feed itself delivers much less than usual. A gap is evidence that AIS was switched off, not proof.

Where do the transit counts come from?

IMF PortWatch derives daily counts from satellite AIS and releases them weekly, so the latest day is often several days old.
